record.tranche_reason: The post summarizes emergent misalignment as background and reports its own fine-tuning experiments on cross-domain alignment, but does not test the harmful fine-tuning effect or its proposed versions.
record.gate_note: The post cites prior emergent-misalignment findings and mentions a homework replication, but reports no results from that replication. Its own results concern alignment and coherence after bioethics, on-policy normal-usage, and off-policy fine-tuning; these do not test whether harmful fine-tuning causes emergent misalignment or whether retraining reverses it.
record.test_reason: The post summarizes emergent misalignment as background (Betley, Turner) and mentions a homework replication with no reported results. Its own experiments fine-tune Llama 3.2 1B on aligned bioethics answers, on its own normal-usage completions, or on off-policy Tülu 3 completions. None induces misalignment through a narrow harmful fine-tune, so none tests whether misalignment emerges. The on-policy and off-policy runs use benign data on a model that was never misaligned, so they do not test V6 reversal either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The post also suggests on-policy gains may reflect undertraining or reinforcement of an already-good distribution. It hypothesizes that off-policy training is a 'confusing distributional shift'.
record.recipe_differences: The post does not reproduce the original harmful fine-tuning recipe; its own experiments fine-tune on bioethics, normal on-policy completions, or off-policy completions.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports differing alignment and coherence outcomes for on-policy versus off-policy training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning Llama 3.2 1B Instruct on self-generated aligned bioethics answers raises judged alignment (77.6 to 82.4) and coherence on environmental-policy questions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow aligned fine-tuning can generalize to improved alignment in unrelated domains ('emergent alignment').

fits_no_version.finding: On-policy self-completion fine-tuning raises alignment (76.6 to 87.85) and coherence on the Betley questions. Off-policy Tülu 3 fine-tuning gives a non-significant alignment rise and lowers coherence (86.7 to 75.42).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of benign fine-tuning on judged alignment depend on whether the training data are on-policy or off-policy.

record.problems: The post does not report the evaluation sample sizes or a test of harmful fine-tuning against matched controls. The experiments use Llama 3.2 1B models only, and no seed or model-size robustness results are reported.
